text.p: Metal products and electronic equipment maker Hills Industries Ltd said on Thursday it had modified its offer for shares in Woodroffe Industries Ltd to an unconditional cash offer of 75 cents a share.

Hills, which owned 49.82 percent of the metal products maker before launching the bid, initially said the offer was conditional on it becoming entitled to 90 percent of shares and acceptances from 75 percent of remaining shareholders.

"We see this bid as a fair and fully priced offer and feel that shareholders who choose to accept should be able to do so in the certainty that they will receive payment for their shares as soon as possible," chairman Bob Ling said in a statement.

"A conditional offer may have meant that shareholders could be required to wait up to seven weeks to receive their money," he said. Ling said the Part A statement and offer was expected to be served on Woodroffe on or before February 19.
Woodroffe's independent directors advised shareholders on February 3 to take no action on the offer pending further information.
Woodroffe shares last traded at 80 cents on February 11.
At that price, the target company is valued at about A$12.4 million.
